analysis.title: Energy & Infrastructure Insight: Power Generation
key_insights: Power has shifted from a financial-markets backwater to a focus theme because AI data center demand makes power capacity a primary constraint on AI growth, per the report.
Independent power producers Constellation Energy (CEG) and Vistra (VST) share prices rose over 500% in the three years to 10/15/25, after forward power curves steepened from May 2023 to May 2024.

Constellation owns about 22,000 MW of nuclear (the nation's largest fleet) plus 11,000 MW of renewable and thermal generation. Vistra manages about 37,000 MW across nuclear, gas, coal, solar, wind and storage. Neither is a rate-regulated utility.

Retail electricity prices rose 14% from May 2023 to the report date, over twice the rate of CPI. They are forecast to rise a further 15-40% by 2030 across various utility service areas, largely on data center demand.

Power prices are determined primarily by natural gas prices and are closely correlated. Forward spark spreads have risen faster than forward power over the last six months, which the report reads as a significant tightening of supply and demand and sharply better profitability for efficient generators.
PJM expects net energy load growth of 4.8% a year over the next decade and ERCOT expects 8.9% a year from 2025-2031. These rates have caught the industry flat-footed on supply response.
McKinsey forecasts data center demand rising from 178 TWh in 2024 (4.3% of U.S. demand, more than New York State's 140 TWh) to 513 TWh by end 2029, a 23.6% CAGR and over 10% of forecast U.S. demand.
Five data centers are scheduled to exceed 1,000 MW each in 2026, versus a largest of about 300 MW a couple of years ago.

Amazon agreed to co-locate a data center next to an existing dual-unit nuclear project under a 10-year, 120 MW+ PPA at well above market prices. Tech companies also sign long-term solar and wind PPAs to meet clean power goals.
Average renewable PPA prices rose 107% from 1Q20 to 3Q25 versus a 17% rise in U.S. inflation.

Interconnection is the most significant constraint on renewables. The queue is over 90% renewables and storage, about 9,000 projects and 1,783 GW, with waits up to five years. Storage and solar-plus-storage are 47% of the queue.

The investment tax credits in place since 1978 are being sunset, but the report says renewable development is not chilled much because project economics have improved and data center timelines favor renewables and storage.

Natural gas projects in the interconnection queue number 693, up from 455 before the current administration took office. The waitlist for gas turbines is 5-7 years, so new gas capacity is a medium to long term supply response.
PJM projects about 40 GW of retirements by 2030, 21% of its 2023 fleet, mostly coal. Coal plants have been minimally maintained, so higher power prices alone may not justify extensions.

The capacity factor of quick-ramping gas peakers has nearly doubled in ten years as intermittent capacity replaced baseload. Peakers earn low margins, which has limited new peaking development despite capacity market rule changes in PJM and state financing support in Texas.

The report expects power prices to keep rising, regional reliability concerns, battery storage driving the energy transition, and constrained new gas generation. Small modular reactors are a wild card with long timelines.

Credit implications: existing generation assets benefit and efficient assets see higher margins. Fixed-price PPA projects do not benefit immediately. The renewable financing pipeline should stay robust, and utility rate cases and allowed returns face more uncertainty in a higher-for-longer rate environment.

market_movers.rationale: Cited as a large merchant generator whose shares rose over 500% in three years on the power demand narrative. The report gives no rating or target.
Cited alongside Constellation as a merchant generator that benefits from rising forward power prices. The report gives no rating or target.

sector_views.rationale: Existing generation assets of all kinds are expected to benefit from rising power prices and a tightening supply stack, with efficient assets seeing higher margins.

macro_indicators.reading: +14% from May 2023 to present, over twice the rate of CPI
macro_indicators.interpretation: Power costs are rising faster than general inflation, driven in large part by data center demand.

macro_indicators.reading: +15-40% by 2030 across various utility service areas
macro_indicators.interpretation: Further large increases in power costs expected, a possible inflation input and a regulatory pressure point.

macro_indicators.reading: 4.8% a year average over the next decade
macro_indicators.interpretation: Grid operator expects strong load growth after decades of flat demand.
Texas expects the fastest load growth, with curtailment and reliability issues in the meantime.

macro_indicators.reading: 178 TWh in 2024 rising to 513 TWh by end 2029 (McKinsey)
macro_indicators.interpretation: A 23.6% CAGR, over 10% of total forecast U.S. electricity demand by 2029.

crypto_views: The report lists cryptocurrency mining among new calls on power capacity, and mentions cryptocurrency ETFs only as a market theme that power had been overshadowed by.
risk_factors: Interconnection queue delays of up to five years limit renewable and storage additions.
Gas turbine waitlists of 5-7 years constrain new gas capacity.
Peaking capacity economics are poor and capacity market mechanisms have proven fickle.
Retirement of about 40 GW of PJM thermal capacity by 2030 strains grid reliability.
Future administrations could retrench support for natural gas, and batteries or small modular reactors could push gas to the margins of the dispatch curve.
Cost allocation for data center load may leave ratepayers with higher bills and no direct benefit.
Rate cases and allowed equity returns face uncertainty in a higher-for-longer rate environment.
Renewable curtailment from transmission constraints, especially in western Texas.

tension_points.bull_case: Gas projects are in a groundswell of interest, with 693 in the interconnection queue, and existing gas plants see an improved outlook as power prices rise.
tension_points.bear_case: Capacity mechanisms have proven fickle, capital costs are high, supply chains are difficult, and new projects carry 30+ year lives. Better batteries or small modular reactors could push gas to the margins of the dispatch curve.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Improved battery storage technology and/or a nuclear renaissance deploying smaller modular reactors, or retrenchment of support by future administrations.

theme_stances.key_argument: Data center expansion is central to the new supply and demand narrative and is driving higher power prices.
theme_stances.evidence: data center expansion is central to the new supply/demand narrative

theme_stances.key_argument: New gas-fired peaking capacity offers the best short-term solution to increased intermittency, but turbine waitlists constrain supply.
theme_stances.evidence: New gas-fired peaking capacity offers the best short-term solution
